newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE March white sugar pushes away from support.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE March white sugar pushes away from support.

text.p: White sugar futures pushed gently higher in modest activity on Tuesday as trade buyers followed the more bullish sentiment in the New York raws market, market sources said. Two leading trade houses were said to be dominating the turnover in London, with some of the purchases believed to be a spillover from Monday's session. Much of the March volume derived from outright dealings, they added.
"There seems to be fairly good outright buying by the trade," said one market source. "The March/May switch has come under a bit of pressure, to around 80 cents."
At 1719 GMT March was $1.90 higher at $302.00 after briefly dipping under nearby support at $300.00. May was up $2.20 at $301.50 and overall volume was 1,805 lots.
Traders said while speculator activity was ruling the New York raws market, most funds already seemed to have liquidated their long positions.
But strength in the March raws drew the spot white/raw premium in by around $1 to $68, which was described as a good selling opportunity.

The London market was still waiting for the result of Libya's tender to buy two cargoes of 45 ICUMSA white sugar for February/March shipment. The final decision on the supplier is expected on Wednesday, European sugar sources said.
Turkish state refiner Turkseker said it was still assessing bids from around 10 companies for a tender under which it will sell up to 50,000 tonnes of white sugar.
London traders said bid prices reported were between $315 and $320 per tonne.
In Paris the market followed a similar trading pattern, with March and May both up by $1.80 at $301.80 and $301.30 respectively. Matif volume totalled a light 305 lots.
